project.title: Sample Residence – Weatherization Audit
project.program: New Jersey Weatherization Assistance Program (DOE WAP, PY 2026) with LIHEAP weatherization funds
project.note: Fictitious house and household. Test results, bills, prices and costs are illustrative values, not customer data.

household.eligibility: Income at 159 % of the HHS poverty guidelines (WAP limit 200 %); LIHEAP recipient 2025–26
household.occupant_notes: Occupant at home all day; bedroom AC window units used in July and August.

dwelling.type: Single-family detached, one-story ranch over full basement
dwelling.description: Wood frame, 2x4 walls with plaster and painted wood clapboard siding, vented attic with flat ceiling, full concrete-block basement inside the thermal boundary (furnace, water heater, laundry, sump pit). Replacement vinyl windows (1990s).

climate.source: Synthetic normal year calibrated to roughly 4,900 HDD65 (central New Jersey) – an approved audit tool uses TMY weather for the nearest station

envelope.name: Ceiling below vented attic
envelope.desc: R-11 fiberglass batts between 2x6 joists, gaps and compression (≈ R-9 effective)

envelope.name: Above-grade walls, net
envelope.desc: 2x4 @ 16" o.c., empty cavities, plaster, board sheathing, clapboard

envelope.name: Exterior doors
envelope.desc: Wood panel front door with storm door, steel rear door

envelope.name: Rim / band joist
envelope.desc: 2x8 rim joist, uninsulated, unsealed sill (142 ft perimeter)

heating.desc: Gas furnace, natural draft (Category I), 80,000 Btu/h input, installed 1996, ducts in basement
heating.efficiency_note: Steady-state efficiency 78.4 % measured with combustion analyzer; nameplate AFUE 78 %
heating.dse_note: Ducts within the basement; leakage at plenums, takeoffs and panned returns; estimated distribution efficiency

dhw.desc: Gas storage water heater, atmospheric (natural draft), 40 gal, installed 2014, UEF 0.58, common vent with furnace

refrigerator.metering: 2-hour metering with logging plug meter, door closed, compressor cycles complete; annualized per state protocol

prices.source: Illustrative marginal residential rates (delivery + supply) – use the client's utility tariff

economics.source: 3.0 % real discount rate (DOE/FEMP, NIST IR 85-3273-40, 2025). Real energy price escalation illustrative – replace with UPV-DOE factors, residential, Middle Atlantic

program.source: DOE WPN 26-1 (PY 2026 adjusted average $8,813); NJ PY 2026 H&S Plan: H&S average 14 % of ACPU, waiver for individual units above $1,500

bills.source: Utility billing history, 12 months (fictitious); HDD65 per billing period from nearest NOAA station

blower_door.setup: Single-point test, house depressurized to −50 Pa with reference to outside, basement door open, attic hatch closed, all exterior openings closed, combustion appliances off, ash/dust check
blower_door.n_factor_note: LBL N-factor for climate zone 4, normal shielding, one story plus basement (illustrative)

caz.vent_group: natural-draft furnace commonly vented with water heater
caz.worst_case_setup: Dryer on, bath/kitchen exhaust none present, air handler on, basement door closed (worst case found), house-to-CAZ pressure measured with manometer
caz.cause: Return-side duct leakage at the furnace cabinet and panned joist returns draws air out of the basement while the air handler runs.

oven.name: Gas range/oven
oven.note: Measured in flue port after 5 minutes at 500 °F

gas_leaks.reading: Combustible gas detector 1,200 ppm at union

duct.pressure_pan: Supply registers 0.3–0.8 Pa, panned returns 1.9 Pa (leaky)
duct.note: Ducts inside the basement; return leakage affects CAZ

radon.method: Charcoal canister test, NJDEP protocol (48 h)
radon.consent: Radon informed consent signed, EPA 'A Citizen's Guide to Radon' provided

caz_limits.source: Action levels as applied in this sample per ANSI/BPI-1200-S-2017 and the NJ PY 2026 H&S Plan (oven 225 ppm as measured, ambient 35 ppm); depressurization limit per the state field guide for commonly vented natural-draft appliances

local_exhaust.note: No exhaust fan; mildew on ceiling

ventilation_62_2.fan_desc: ENERGY STAR bath fan, 80 cfm boost on occupancy/humidity sensor, continuous low speed 40 cfm, ducted to exterior with backdraft damper
ventilation_62_2.source: ASHRAE 62.2-2016 with Normative Appendix A (existing buildings); weather and shielding factor wsf illustrative – NJ requires the RED ASHRAE 62.2-2016 calculator with target and final blower door readings

measures.name: Air sealing – attic bypasses and basement
measures.location: Attic floor, basement sill and penetrations
measures.spec: Seal attic bypasses before insulating: top plates, plumbing stack and wiring penetrations, chimney chase (sheet metal and high-temperature sealant, maintain clearance to masonry), attic hatch weatherstrip. Basement: sill plate to foundation, utility penetrations. Guided by blower door; target listed under test targets.

lines.item: Materials: one-part foam, caulk, rigid board, high-temp sealant, sheet metal

measures.name: Attic insulation to R-49
measures.spec: Blow cellulose over existing batts to R-49 total, uniform depth, depth rulers every 300 ft², certificate posted at hatch. Dam and insulate hatch, baffles at every soffit bay, keep 3 in. clearance to chimney and non-IC fixtures (dam).

lines.item: Attic hatch dam and rigid foam on hatch

measures.name: Wall insulation – dense-pack cellulose
measures.spec: Drill-and-fill from exterior through clapboard: remove one course, drill 2-9/16" holes into every cavity (above and below windows, check fire blocking), dense-pack cellulose at ≥ 3.5 lb/ft³, plug, reinstall siding. Verify fill with infrared scan or density check. Lead-safe work practices (see H&S).

lines.item: Dense-pack cellulose, drill and fill from exterior
Replace split clapboards at drill line, prime

measures.name: Rim joist insulation and sealing
measures.spec: 2 in. closed-cell spray foam (≈ R-13) on rim joist and sill, sealing sill-to-foundation joint. Install per manufacturer's evaluation report; thermal or ignition barrier as required by code.

measures.name: Duct sealing – supply and return in basement
measures.location: Basement: furnace cabinet, plenums, takeoffs, panned returns
measures.spec: Seal return plenum, filter slot (cover), cabinet seams and panned joist returns with mastic and fabric; seal supply plenum and takeoffs. Re-test CAZ worst case with air handler on.
measures.hs_fallback: Return-side duct leakage depressurizes the CAZ (worst case −3.8 Pa against a −3.0 Pa limit, water heater spills 95 s). Sealing is required to correct the combustion safety failure.

measures.name: Furnace replacement – 95 % AFUE sealed combustion
measures.spec: Replace 1996 natural-draft furnace with 95 % AFUE two-pipe sealed-combustion furnace sized by Manual J; line chimney for the orphaned water heater.

lines.item: Chimney liner for orphaned water heater

measures.name: Low-flow showerhead 1.5 gpm
measures.spec: WaterSense showerhead 1.5 gpm; leave old showerhead with client only on request.

measures.name: Water heater pipe insulation
measures.spec: Insulate first 6 ft of hot and cold pipe at the water heater (keep 6 in. clearance from draft hood/flue); verify setpoint 120–125 °F.

measures.name: LED lamps
measures.spec: Replace remaining incandescent and CFL lamps with ENERGY STAR LED of equal lumen output.

measures.name: Refrigerator replacement (metered)
measures.spec: ENERGY STAR top-freezer, 18 cu ft, label ≤ 385 kWh/yr; haul away old unit to a certified recycler (refrigerant recovery), keep disposal receipt in client file.

lines.item: ENERGY STAR refrigerator 18 cu ft, delivered
Removal and recycling of old unit

health_safety.item: Gas leak at furnace gas cock union
health_safety.finding: Combustible gas detector 1,200 ppm at union, customer side of the meter
health_safety.action: HVAC technician to remake union, leak-test all furnace connections with CGD and soap solution; occupant informed in writing

health_safety.finding: Vinyl foil duct crushed and partly disconnected, lint in basement (fire and moisture hazard)
health_safety.action: Install rigid metal duct, foil tape (no screws), exterior hood with damper; clean lint

lines.item: Dryer vent, rigid metal, exterior hood

health_safety.finding: No bathroom exhaust, mildew on bath ceiling; local exhaust deficits kitchen and bath
health_safety.action: Install the fan described under ventilation, duct to exterior (insulated duct in attic, roof or gable cap with damper), measure flow at both speeds

lines.item: Bath fan with continuous/boost controls, ducting, wiring

health_safety.finding: No CO alarm; hallway smoke alarm dated 2012 (beyond manufacturer's lifetime)
health_safety.action: Install combination smoke/CO alarm in the hallway outside bedrooms and a CO alarm in the basement; explain operation

health_safety.finding: Open sump pit in basement; radon test 1.6 pCi/L (below 4.0 action level)
health_safety.action: Airtight sump pit cover with sealed penetrations, seal slab cracks and floor penetrations

lines.item: Airtight sump cover, sealing of floor penetrations

health_safety.finding: House built before 1978, painted clapboard and plaster (lead presumed)
health_safety.action: EPA RRP lead-safe practices for drilling siding and any interior disturbance: containment, HEPA cleanup, cleaning verification, records

lines.item: RRP setup, containment and cleaning verification

deferral_screen: Mildew < 10 ft² on bath ceiling – cleaned, addressed by HS-3
No vermiculite in attic; duct tape is foil (no suspect ACM)
